# Future Breakdown of Cohort

- So I previously got all 1.2 million Crohn's PatientDurableKeys,in the recipe PatientWithDx. I now want to upload that and then get lots more info - med tables, visit tables, etc. Given the size, I thought it was going to be a huge upload, taking a long time, and that it be a major time sink in relation to doing a large poll. It turns out that it wasn't the case. It took about two minutes to do the upload of 1.2 million rows with probably ten columns. I think this changes our paradigm of trying to get the whole cohort together.

  - Previous wisdom was that if I had a multiplier I should do all the runs of one cohort together while Cosmos connection is still up. Now I see I don't have to - I could do somethign as simple as a new open connection every table if I wanted to! Of course, some tables rely on other pulle dtables, and they' often have a theme (say, the 3 medication tables), so I dont' want to group a few more than one table together. The added benefit is that I can see how it's going mid-batch, which I couldn't do either and led me to understand if soemthing was never finishing.

  - I'm now thinking we can have recipes that are multiple tables - maybe a new column called 'cohort recipes', which I could do like 'medicaitons' and have multiple tables under it. It could work like a mini cohort table, essentially, and have the same variable-based connections that everythign else does. Ideas include like medication info, visit info, birthing info, things that tend to have two or three different tables that are connected to each other in some way.

- I think this is a little more like what I had intended to do in the original set, but was afraid of the sort of cohort upload block being this huge delay. I think now we can look at it more flexibly. Say there are 9 tables, 3 in a birth block (birth fact, mother info, pregnancy fact/dim), 3 in a med block (med order, admin, dispense), visits block (edvisits, hospitaladmissions, etc.). Say I have a multiplier of, say, 'IBD' - UC, Crohns. Well if I get the PK table for all of UC, then I can move through the three blocks as their own batch, so that way we can say "getting UC Meds block" instead of "getting all UC data".

- For the UI, the question is where to place this. IN splitter, I actually think this may be a bit confusing right now, because 'separate tables' currently means meaning that the splitter duplicates the tables for a new splitter variable. Instead, that should be renamed to 'separate PKs per splitter', or something like that. Then, this table batch option could be 'group tables into a batch' and then once it's opened, you can just add different groups, give them a group name, and then it has an 'add table to group' oand 'remove table from group' and 'remove group' buttons. It should say that 'anything left over will be its own group batch' or something.

- i want to ensure the current features work first. BuTo that end, tell me your questions, so we have mutual understanding. ONce taht's done, outline the findings to 'roadmap' so we can make this the first feature add as soon as the pulls are successfully running.

::: {.callout-note title="🟦 Claude: groups at run time"}
**What the code does today.** A session is one Cosmos connection, held open from setup to its last run (D36), because every `##` temp dies with it. It has one PK, and each multiplier level gets its own session. Inside it: setup, uploads, the PK, then one run per batch (chunks inside the run), each table built, landed in Projects and committed before the next (D55). Nothing runs in parallel.

Two things already outlive a connection: the PK's Projects copy, which every batch refills the PK temp from (D18, D19), and each upload's `upload_<dest>` copy. So a group in a fresh connection needs its PK temp refilled from Projects, which costs about what your 2-minute upload did, plus the supporting tables it reads. Nothing else is needed, **as long as it reads no table another group made**. Your idea fits the runtime as a new level: session (one PK, built once) → **group (one connection)** → batch → chunk. With no groups, a session is one group, which is exactly today.

**Questions:**

1.  **Which leg took two minutes?** An uploaded PK travels twice: file to Projects, then Projects to the Cosmos temp through the client. A new connection repeats only the second. If you don't know, Crohns_PatientsFromUpload's log will say.
2.  **What do you want from a group:** its own connection (a stuck or failed group costs only itself, and the next one still runs), a name in the progress ("UC · Meds · c3of12"), or both? And what could you not see mid-batch? Each table is already committed as it lands, so the log should say so. If it was the Crohn's run, that was one unjoined medication query (above), which no grouping would have split.
3.  **A table that reads another group's table** (a visit table joined to a medication table): its temp is gone once the other group's connection closes. **Recommendation:** an error naming both groups ("put them in one group"), rather than quietly reloading it from Projects.
4.  **Which is outer, groups or batches?** (a) Group outside: every chunk of UC Meds, then every chunk of UC Visits, one connection per group. (b) Batch outside: chunk 1's meds and visits, then chunk 2's. "Getting UC Meds block" reads as (a). **Recommendation:** (a).
5.  **Leftovers:** do the tables in no group share one group (one connection, as today), or does each get its own? **Recommendation:** one shared group, so a template with no groups runs exactly as now. A table can still be put in a group of its own.

I'll assume, unless you say otherwise, that a failed group is retried alone (`--retry-failed`) while finished groups are skipped, and that under `Dual` every SneakPeek session still runs first.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="🟦 Claude: cohort recipes"}
**What the code does today.** Each entry under `recipes:` in `reference/recipes.yaml` is one table. A recipe that reads another generated table names it through a variable (`{{prefix}}_{{HospitalICDTable}}`), a table input, which the template must bind on the table; an unbound one is an error that names the tables that fit, and nothing is bound for you (D45).

**Questions:**

6.  **How are a set's tables connected?** This matters most. Is MedicationAdministrationFact pulled *for the orders already pulled* (a chain: the order table first, then the others joined to it), or is each of the three joined to the PK on its own? Birth sounds like a chain (the birth, then its mother, then the pregnancy), meds perhaps not. A chain needs one connection and an order inside the group; independent tables need neither.
7.  **What does adding "Medications" put in the template?** **Recommendation:** its tables as ordinary fact tables, each editable and removable as a prefabricated table is now, with their table inputs to each other already bound, and a group holding them. After that, nothing special: it is not one unit you edit as a whole.
8.  **Is a cohort recipe the same thing as a group?** **Recommendation:** no, two things. A recipe set brings a group with it, but you can move its tables out, and group hand-built tables with no recipe.
9.  **Variables:** do a set's tables share any (a date window for all three medication tables, say), set once for the set? **Recommendation:** not at first. They take the template's and the PK's variables, as every table does now.
10. **Where sets are kept and made:** a new `recipe_sets:` list in `recipes.yaml`, with a **Save as recipe set** on a group in the app, as Save as Recipe works for one table?
:::

::: {.callout-note title="🟦 Claude: names and where it goes in the app"}
**What the code does today.** Splitters offers **Separate tables** (`split_after_build`: each level its own PK, session and tables, such as blackPatients and whitePatients, with an optional control) and **Pieces of one table** (batching: the rows land in one table, each labelled in a `_batch` column).

**Questions:**

11. **Rename "Separate tables"** to **"Separate PK per level"**? Its tables are separate too, so "Separate PK and tables per level" is the fuller version.
12. **The word "batch" is taken.** Batching already means pieces of one table, and every destination has a `_batch` column. **Recommendation:** call these **table groups** in the app ("Add group", "Add table to group", "Remove group"), or **blocks**, your word for birth, meds and visits.
13. **Where it goes.** A group gathers tables, not pieces of the PK, and needs the tables to exist first. **Recommendation:** its own section after Fact Tables, with the note "Tables in no group run together, as one group", and each fact table saying which group it is in.
:::
